Trying to compile a list of lyrical *references*! (Credits to GreaterOrEqual0 for original compilation)
0:06 Circuits: Originated from ML Interpretability, the hypothesis that nodes in a neural network are grouped by the functions they perform. Each group is known as a circuit
0:10 Sudden drop in training loss: Potential reference to grokking/double descent (?)
0:23 p(doom): the estimated percentage probability that artificial intelligence will cause an existential catastrophe, such as human extinction or societal collapse
0:25 FOOM: Of unknown origin, a sudden increase in AI capabilities (compare: boom)
0:27 Chinese Room: A thought experiment, See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_room. The Chinese room argument holds that a computer executing a program cannot have a mind, understanding, or consciousness, regardless of how intelligently or human-like the program may make the computer behave.
0:30 Shoggoth: Originally a Twitter meme, the depiction of LLMs as a monstrous alien creature with a smiley face plastered on. Also, Shoggoth is originally from an H. P. Lovecraft story, it’s an engineered lifeform intended to serve its creators, but ended up destroying them.
0:34 Shinigami eyes: Originally from anime Death Note, the supernatural ability to see the remaining lifespan of other humans. In Japanese, means God of Death. (Shini-death)(kami-God).
0:43 Singularity: Popularized by Ray Kurzweil, a hypothetical event where technological progress accelerates beyond human control
0:50 Atoms rearranging: Originally a joke about tigers, the idea that superhuman AI "doesn't want to eat you, it only wants to help rearrange your atoms"!
0:53 Sydney: An early chatbot by Microsoft in 2023, famous for exhibiting psychotic behaviors to its users and was shut down consequently
1:01 Roko's basilisk: A thought experiment of an AI that punishes anyone who knows of its potential existence but does not contribute to building it
1:02 NVDA to the moon is also about the Nvidia stock rising with the AI bubble for those who don’t invest
1:05 Omega Point: a theoretical end-state where the universe converges into a final point of maximum complexity, consciousness, and unification
1:07 1e30 flops: It was rumored that GPT-4 took 10^30 FLOPs to train (?)
1:15 MLPs: Multi-Layer Perceptrons, the basic architecture of neural networks. Funnily enough, Transformers are not MLPs
1:18 von Neumann: The basic architecture of computers since the 1940s. Criticized as inefficient for AI training
1:26 Critical Design Review(?): A process in software engineering to check if a system design is mature enough to build
1:26 - CDR is probably  Cloud Detection and Response, "a cybersecurity approach that identifies and responds to cyberthreats across all cloud layers"
1:30 Gato: An AI system created by DeepMind in 2022. Not notable
1:38 Paperclip Maximizer: A thought experiment that an AI trained to maximize paperclip production will end up destroying the world in the process of doing so
1:39 Killswitch: Originally a Twitter meme, the rumor that OpenAI was hiring a "Killswitch Engineer" to pull the plug on GPT-5 if things go awry
1:46 Orthogonality Thesis: Due to Nick Bostrom, the hypothesis that the level of intelligence of an AI is independent of its "final goal"
1:50 "Transformers all the way!": Based off the "Turtles all the way down."  Turtles all the way down" is an idiom that describes an infinite regress, meaning a chain of reasoning, support, or explanation that never reaches a final foundation and instead goes on forever. The phrase comes from a famous anecdote where a scientist or philosopher gives a lecture about how the Earth orbits the Sun. Afterward, an elderly audience member claims the Earth is actually flat and rests on the back of a giant turtle. When asked what that turtle stands on, she replies, "You're very clever, young man, but it's turtles all the way down!"—meaning each turtle stands on an even bigger turtle, with no bottom layer.
• The Philosophical Point: It highlights the problem of how we justify knowledge. If every reason requires a prior reason, and that reason requires another, where does the chain stop?
1:56 Post-Chinchilla: Refers to the Chinchilla Scaling Law, the idea that you should train a smaller model and spend more tokens on inference
2:01 RLHF: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback, the basic aligning paradigm of LLMs since GPT-3.5
2:07 Loom: An early LLM interface that structured a conversation as a tree, not a linear sequence
2:13 "What did Ilya see?": Originally a Twitter meme, refers to the OpenAI boardroom crisis in 2023. It was rumored that OpenAI cofounder Ilya Sutskever saw a secret AGI breakthrough in the lab which made him fire Sam Altman. The real reason for the firing, however, was nothing more than corporate politics.
